idiom_name: Spring Kafka KafkaTemplate.executeInTransaction (JVM) / Exposed newSuspendedTransaction + outbox
implementation_notes: Kotlin reaches the same JVM transaction supply as Java - JTA/XA with a transacted JMS Session, Spring Kafka's transactional KafkaTemplate, or a container-managed @Transactional - so the transaction boundary must stay with the JVM transaction manager and not with a coroutine scope. Kotlin adds access idioms rather than semantics: lambda-scoped boundaries, and coroutine-friendly database code such as Exposed's newSuspendedTransaction for the local-transaction realization (outbox row plus relay). Because the supply is shared, this file records one realization and leaves the JTA-versus-Spring-Kafka split to the Java sibling.
pitfalls: newSuspendedTransaction runs on its own JDBC connection and commits by itself; writing the outbox row there while expecting the surrounding JTA transaction to commit it splits the commit and recreates the dual write.
A blocking JTA commit called from a coroutine blocks a dispatcher thread unless the call is dispatched to Dispatchers.IO.
Coroutine cancellation between staging and commit aborts the transaction, so the commit step belongs in withContext(NonCancellable) when the unit of work must complete.
